SINACA Mayor Municipality of Malimono Province Of Surigao del Norte Dear Mayor Sinaca: This refers to your letter dated April 12, 2022, requesting the Department's legal opinion in relation to the following: (1) SB Appropriation Ordinance No. 01, series of 2023, titled "An Ordinance Authorizing the Revised Annual Budget of Malimono Municipal Government for Fiscal Year 2023 in the Total Amount of One Hundred Twenty-Three Million Twenty-Eight Thousand Seventy-Three Pesos (Php Covering the Various Expenditures for the Operation of the Municipal Government for Fiscal Year 2023 and Appropriating the Necessary Funds for the Purpose"; and (2) SB Resolution No. 88 series of 2023, which overrides your veto dated April 2023. Hereunder are the factual antecedents as represented in your letter: • The Appropriation Ordinance approving and/or authorizing the Proposed Executive Budget for the fiscal year 2023 was already passed and enacted on December 29, 2022 but such enactment was not transmitted by the Vice Mayor or by the Sanggunian Secretary to the Office of the Municipal Mayor as required by law; • There were two appropriation ordinances passed and enacted by the sanggunian: First, it was on December 29, 2022 and second, it was allegedly on March 6, 2023; • You are of the view that the non-transmittal of such an approved ordinance is an utter disregard of the SB Internal Rules of Procedurel, which provide that "the measure is deemed approved by the sanggunian. The Secretary certifies the measure is correct and the Presiding Officer signs it before it is transmitted to the LCE for approval." • The second Appropriation Ordinance allegedly enacted on March 6, 2023, exceeded I RULE IX (Legislative Process) SB Internal Rules of Procedure, Section 32 (Rules in the Enactment Of Ordinances and Adoption of Resolutions). The Secretary certifies the measure correct and the Presiding Officer signs it before it is transmitted to the LCE Ior approval. Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No,: 8876-34-54

the total Proposed Executive Budget for fiscal year 2023 by Php 126,000.00, contravening Article 415 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Code). • Parenthetically, the SB created new line items not found in the proposed executive budget for the fiscal year 2023, which was approved as early as December 29, 2022. In its resolution overriding your veto, it still apportioned the whole appropriation for the LDRRMO I to provide funds for the Indigenous Mandatory Representative (IPMR); • It has slashed amounts of appropriation from the MDRRMO Office and the Mayor's Office and also considerably increased the SB appropriation on its personal services, amounting to Php3,078,388.16, which resulted in an excess of the total proposed executive budget for fiscal year 2023 by Php 126,000.00; • The Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP), through SP Resolution No. 119, series of 2023, disapproved the abolition of Municipal Government Department Head I (LDRRMO) with Salary Grade 24: • You contend that the slashed amount in the proposed executive budget—as gleaned from the second appropriation ordinance allegedly enacted on March 6, 2023, amounting to Phpl squarely not appropriate under the prevailing circumstances; • Said SP Resolution was, however, ignored by the sanggunian through SB Resolution NO. 88, series of 2023. Premised from the foregoing antecedents, the following issues are proffered for this Department's legal opinion: 1. Whether it is proper to pass and enact another appropriation ordinance despite the passage and enactment of an appropriation ordinance as early as December 29, 2022; 2. Whether an appropriation ordinance that was already passed and enacted/approved in the third reading can still be changed by the sanggunian instead of being transmitted to the office of the municipal mayor for approval; 3. Whether it is proper for a sanggunian to disregard a sangguniang panlalawigan's disapproval of a municipal ordinance; 4. Whether the sanggunian can legally increase the proposed amount of appropriation in the executive budget; and 5. Whether the sanggunian can validly enact an appropriation ordinance without consultation with the local finance committee? We shall answer the foregoing issues in seriatim. We note that the first and second queries pertain to the same subject matter, and hence, we deemed it apt and wise to address both queries in one discussion. Foremost, it is to be noted that while the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code) has a specific chapter regarding local legislation2, the same is bereft of clear provisions regarding the dynamic of the local legislative process. Be that as it may, the Code granted the sanggunian authority to adopt its own internal rules of procedure (IRP), which include, among others, the conduct of its legislative process. In particular, Section 50 thereof provides: "Section 50. Internal Rules of Procedure. - (a) On the first regular session following the election of its members and Within 2 Chapter Ill (Legal Legislation) Local Government Code of 1991 Page 2 of 2

ninety (90) days thereafter, the sanggunian concerned shall adopt or update its existing rules of procedure. (b) The rules of procedure shall provided for the following: (1) The organization of the sanggunian and the election of its officers as well as the creation of standing committees which shall include, but shall not be limited to, the committees on appropriations, women and family, human rights, youth and sports development, environmental protection, and cooperatives; the general jurisdiction of each committee; and the election of the chairman and members of each committee; (2) The order and calendar of business for each session; (3) The legislative process; (4) The parliamentary procedures which include the conduct Of members during sessions; (5) The discipline of members for disorderly behavior and absences without justifiable cause for four (4) consecutive sessions, for which they may be censured, reprimanded, or excluded from the session, suspended for not more than sixty (60) days, or expelled: Provided, That the penalty of suspension or expulsion shall require the concurrence of at least two-thirds (2/3) vote of all the sanggunian members: Provided, further, That a member convicted by final judgment to imprisonment of at least one (1) year for any crime involving moral turpitude shall be automatically expelled from the sanggunian; and (6) Such other rules as the sanggunian may adopt." (Emphasis supplied) Accordingly, the local legislative process, insofar as it is not provided in the Code, should be governed by the sanggunian's duly adopted IRP. It is to be emphasized that an IRP—as has been clarified by this Department time and time again—is merely designed for the orderly and convenient conduct of the proceedings in the sanggunian. Furthermore, the Supreme Court, in one case, held that internal rules are merely procedural and not substantive. It is equally important to emphasize that IRP must be consistent with the Code and other pertinent laws. In the present case, Rule IX of the IRP of the herein concerned sanggunian deals with its legislative process. Specifically, Section 32 thereof provides that the measure, such as the appropriation ordinance in question, is deemed approved by the sanggunian. The Secretary certifies the measure is correct, and the Presiding Officer signs it before it is transmitted to the Local Chief Executive (LCE) for approval. Parenthetically, Section 54 (a) of the Code expressly provides that: "Section 54. Approval Of Ordinances. - (a) Every ordinance enacted by the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan shall be presented to the provincial governor or city or municipal mayor, as the case may be. If the local chief executive concerned approves the same, he shall affix his signature on each and every page thereof; otherwise, he shall veto it and return the same with his objections to the sanggunian, which may proceed to reconsider the page 2 of 3

same. The sanggunian concerned may override the veto of the local chief executive by two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance or resolution effective for all legal intents and purposes." (Emphasis supplied) Clearly, the Code mandates the sanggunian to present its enacted ordinance to the local chief executive for the latter's consideration thereof. Accordingly, this Department submits that the act of the herein concerned sanggunian in enacting another appropriation ordinance appears to be untenable. The legislative process vis-å-vis the enactment of the appropriation ordinance on December 29, 2022, is deemed to have been completed, and thus the local chief executive's consideration of the proposed appropriation ordinance should take its course. We can only surmise what prompted the herein concerned sanggunian to not transmit the appropriation ordinance it enacted in December 2022 and instead enact another appropriation ordinance. At any rate, this Department maintains its position that such action is not proper—granted that there has been an issue in the first appropriation ordinance and this has prompted the herein concerned sanggunian to enact another appropriation ordinance, the same is legislatively improper and finds no legal basis. Any issues should have been addressed during the deliberation of such an ordinance the same must be answered in the negative. This Department submits that it is not proper for the sangguniang bayan to disregard a sangguniang panlalawigan's disapproval of a municipal ordinance. If the sangguniang bayan is not satisfied with the action or decision of the sangguniang panlalawigan vis- a-vis the review of its ordinance, then it should bring the matter before the proper court—this is the proper course of remedy—and not ignore the decision of the sangguniang panlalawigan. Well-settled is the rule that an ordinance passed by a municipality or component city must be validated as consistent with the law through a review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Now, disregarding the decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan puts to naught the legislative intent of mandating the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to review such an ordinance as enunciated under Section 56 of the Code. As regards the fourth issue, this Department has, time and again, opined that, as a general rule, the sanggunian cannot legally increase the proposed amount in the executive budget. Our view is anchored on Article 415 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations, thus: "Article 415. Budget Authorization Xxx The local sanggunian may not increase the proposed amount in the executive budget nor include new items except to provide for statutory and contractual obligations but in no case shall it exceed the total appropriations in the executive budget." (Emphasis supplied) Coming now to the last issue, this Department recognizes the vital role of the Local Finance Committee—established under Section 316 of the Code—vis-å-vis the enactment of the local government appropriation ordinance. In fact, Section 318 of the Code mandates the local chief executive to prepare the executive budget based,

among others, on the estimates of income and budgetary ceilings from the local finance committee. While the critical role of the local finance committee in the preparation of the local government appropriation ordinance cannot be overemphasized, the failure of the sanggunian to consult the local finance committee does not operate to invalid the authority of the sanggunian to enact an appropriation ordinance. Notwithstanding, we would like to reiterate that this Department—being an agency under the executive branch of the government— is devoid of authority to declare invalid or illegal any legislative measure enacted or passed by local government officials, nor does it have authority to declare invalid or illegal any acts committed by local government officials that are alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code or any other applicable laws. The same must be threshed out in the proper forum. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, uthority of the Secretary: By o UAN VICTOR R.
